Yes. Right after rewriting quantize_bvh for the child-pair layout I noticed the new code referenced kInvalidNode, which I did not remember being defined anywhere, so I ran (message #140):

    grep -rn 'kInvalidNode' src/pt_bvh.cpp include/*.hpp | head
    grep -n 'constexpr\|static const' src/pt_bvh.cpp | head

It showed exactly one hit — src/pt_bvh.cpp:399, `std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);` — which was the line I had just written myself inside the new quantize_bvh. There was no declaration in src/pt_bvh.cpp or in any header under include/, so the symbol was undefined and the build would fail. The second grep listed only `21:constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;`, confirming the file had no invalid-node sentinel and showing the file-local `constexpr` style its constants use.

That is what led me, in messages #141-#143, to add `constexpr unsigned int kInvalidNode = 0xFFFFFFFFu;` immediately after kInfinity, after which the child-pair build compiled (aside from the separate PtBvhNodeQ leftover in pt_metal_host.hpp). How I know: this is my own logged action and its tool result, archived at messages #139-#143 and re-read just now from the archive (message #140 holds the command and its verbatim output).
